subject: On‑site validation & nodeclass + NAS retention alignment for Novalabs private cluster
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novalabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, neha_kapoor, marissa_cole
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novalabs private cluster — initial nodeclass + storage intake

Hi Sanjay — great to speak on Friday. Following up with a compact intake so we can align the sprint‑zero prep before field work next month. I copied Karthik and Neha for technical and security alignment, and Marissa for delivery scheduling.

High level asks / constraints we captured:
- Rack footprint: 2 x 42U racks available in site A (power/cool confirmed).
- Networking: single cross‑connect, 10Gbps to customer core; BGP announced via on‑prem router (we'll need VLANs).
- Storage: customer currently offers a shared NFS appliance (NetApp) + 2 x block volumes from on‑prem SAN. No object store on site.
- Retention policy: primary requirement is 90d warm retention for models and 3yr cold archive offsite (S3/partner).
- Compliance: SOC2 scope in play; KMS integration required for secrets and disk encryption.

Proposed technical approach (draft):
1) Nodeclass mapping:
   - mgmt (3x m.curie-small) — control plane and infra pods (ETCD co‑located on dedicated SSD PV with replication)
   - gpu-cache (4x c.gpu-nvme) — local NVMe for model KV cache and ephemeral tensor scratch
   - worker-block (6x c.cpu-block) — block PV mounted for long‑running model artifacts and checkpointing
2) Storage layout:
   - Use local NVMe for runtime caches (no networked PV) to bound latency.
   - Map SAN block volumes to PV classes with zone‑aware replication for model artifacts (read heavy).
   - Expose NFS for shared config and small artifacts only; avoid using NFS for heavy tokenized model storage due to locking/IOPS variability.
3) PV classes & QoS: propose two PV classes: fast-block-replicated (IOPS / RWX as needed) and cache-local (local‑ssd, ephemeral).
4) Encryption & KMS: disk encryption at LUKS level with KMS in customer's HSM; we'll provide integration playbook.

Attachments: sprint-zero checklist and a draft nodeclass CSV to review.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Novalabs can provision a 2nd crossconnect for redundancy and whether the NetApp can export NFS with NFSv4 locks enabled? If Procurement wants an IO‑SLA statement we'll loop Marissa.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo — and thanks to the team for the clear list. Quick answers from our side:  
- We can confirm the two 42U racks and the single 10Gb cross‑connect today. A second cross‑connect is possible but will need procurement sign‑off (cost/time).
- NetApp is currently NFSv4 capable; I will confirm NFSv4 locks by EOD tomorrow.
- For retention: we must keep model artifacts on‑site for 60–90 days (compliant with our audit), then lifecycle to our cloud cold archive (we'll provide S3 credentials for that lifecycle).
- Procurement is copied — they asked for a short IO/SLA statement and an outline of who will be responsible for on‑site hardware diagnostics vs. Redwood field engineers.

Minor constraint: on the SAN we have a QoS policy that throttles sustained writes above 300MB/s per LUN during peak hours (18:00–02:00 local). If your design expects heavy checkpointing during peak hours, we might need to schedule throttled maintenance windows.

Happy to take a 30m call this week to align on the IO profile and to triage which PVs need replication.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Novalabs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novalabs private cluster — initial nodeclass + storage intake

+1 to Mateo's approach. A few technical proposals to make the design resilient and cheaper:  
- Nodeclass detail: name the classes explicitly so PVBinding and scheduling rules are unambiguous: nodeclass-mgmt, nodeclass-gpu-cache, nodeclass-worker-block, nodeclass-spot-burst (for noncritical CI).
- Caching layout: put model shard KV into the gpu-cache local NVMe (hostPath or local PV with LVM wrapper) to avoid NFS jitter. Keep checkpoints on worker-block PV (replicated SAN LUNs).
- NAS strategy: allow NFS only for small config and shared artifacts (RWX). For anything > 10GB or heavy concurrent access, use block PVs. We'll add an operator (rook/csi) only if the site allows object-style interface; otherwise avoid additional control plane components.
- Eviction and preemption: define podDisruptionBudgets for stateful workloads and use PodPriority + node taints to ensure checkpointing jobs do not preempt cached GPU pods.

Action items for me: draft exact PVC templates (sizes + iops targets), a proposed StorageClass YAML, and a short note on scheduling windows for heavy writes to avoid the SAN QoS throttle. I'll attach PV class mapping and the PVC templates in the next email.

karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novalabs private cluster — initial nodeclass + storage intake

Couple of security/ops checks before we lock the PV plan:  
- KMS: need confirmation that Novalabs HSM supports the API handshake we expect (KMIP v2.0). If not, we'll run an envelope encryption flow with a customer‑managed KMS proxy.
- Network segmentation: will the cluster be in a VLAN with egress controls? We should model egress rules for telemetry and image pulls (we prefer staging image registry mirror in the customer network).
- Audit & logs: define retention for prometheus/elastic (we recommend 365d for metrics, 30d for application logs by default). If SOC2 requires longer, we can export to Novalabs SIEM.

Attached a cleaned PDF of the PV class mapping Karthik mentioned and a short checklist for nodeclass burn‑in. Irene — can you confirm whether the on‑site router can announce two BGP prefixes (one teardown suffix we use for canary traffic)?

Neha
Security & Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and owners so Procurement can have the IO/SLA statement and we can schedule the field run: 

1) Novalabs (Sanjay / Procurement): confirm NFSv4 locks and whether a second cross‑connect can be ordered. Provide expected SAN write pattern (average and 95p) for the model checkpoint window (we need numbers to size throttling windows). Target: respond by EOD Thu 18 Apr.
2) Karthik: produce PVC templates, StorageClass YAML, and a small script for NVMe hostPath to local PV conversion. Deliverable by Fri 19 Apr.
3) Neha / Irene: confirm KMIP support and BGP multi‑prefix capability; list any egress firewall rules that will block registry mirrors.
4) Marissa: draft IO/SLA one‑pager and cost note for second cross‑connect; coordinate procurement questions.

I attached the sprint‑zero checklist, a compact pv‑class mapping PDF, and the nodeclass CSV. Once the procurement piece is covered we'll lock the field week and reserve Redwood field engineers for validation (3x FTE, two days).

Proposed meeting: Thu 18 Apr 2029 10:00–10:30 PT — 30m call to review SAN metrics and confirm the cross‑connect timeline. Please ack.

Thanks — Mateo
